tier_rationale: Manufacturer's own product page states plainly that this grill 'is not equipped with WiFIRE® connectivity,' and it ships with Traeger's Digital Arc Controller — a dial-and-display unit with no radio — rather than the WiFi-equipped D2 Controller used on Traeger's Pro and Ironwood lines. Traeger demonstrably files FCC grants for its WiFi-enabled controllers and accessories (grantee 2AZAM), so the vendor's own explicit 'not equipped' statement is corroborated rather than just unsearched.
the_unplug_test: There is no router this grill has ever known about. Fill the hopper, flip the power switch, turn the dial to a temperature, and the auger, igniter and fan run the whole cook exactly as they would in a house with no internet at all. Nothing is lost, because nothing was ever connected.

repairability.notes: Traeger sells replacement Digital Arc controllers, meat probes, and hopper/auger parts directly; the controller is a bolt-on module rather than an integrated board.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page states this grill 'is not equipped with WiFIRE® connectivity,' names the Digital Arc controller, and lists current price $499.99, 300 sq in cooking area, 8 lb hopper, and 120V AC power with no mention of any account or app requirement.

Sibling-control check: grantee 2AZAM (Traeger Pellet Grills LLC) holds FCC grants for its WiFi-enabled controllers and accessories (e.g. an induction cooktop, a wireless meat thermometer for WiFIRE grills), establishing that Traeger files when a product has a radio, which makes the manufacturer's 'not equipped with WiFIRE' statement for the Tailgater meaningful rather than an unchecked claim.

open_questions: Did not confirm directly on fccid.io that no grant exists specifically for the Digital Arc controller module; relied on the manufacturer's own explicit connectivity statement plus the sibling-grant pattern rather than an exhaustive grantee-wide search, to conserve budget.
notes: Published as the D0 half of a same-brand pair with traeger-pro-575: identical company, same 'wood pellet grill and smoker' category, differing only in which controller module is bolted on — the model-number-is-the-whole-story pattern PRINCIPLES calls out. Grill was an empty subcategory before this record.
